executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas represents a persistent elevated zoonotic threat with pandemic potential, flagged across multiple reporting cycles. Vector-borne diseases including dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever continue to surge across the Americas, while mpox transmission persists in the region. Respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis are showing elevated activity with simultaneous co-circulation increasing healthcare burden.
bottomLine: The Americas face a complex multi-threat landscape dominated by H5N1 zoonotic spillover risk, resurgent vector-borne diseases, and co-circulating respiratory pathogens, requiring coordinated One Health surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing spread
Zoonotic spillover events in the Americas with pandemic potential
Sustained animal-human interface risk requiring continuous monitoring
BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in humans
threats.action: Activate enhanced One Health surveillance at animal-human interfaces; enforce biosafety protocols at farms and live poultry markets; prepare pandemic contingency plans and antiviral stockpiles

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission
Continued circulation in the Americas following global clade expansion
BSL-3 select agent with potential for sustained human-to-human transmission
Risk of importation and spread in under-vaccinated populations
threats.action: Expand mpox vaccination coverage in high-risk groups; strengthen case detection and contact tracing; ensure BSL-3 laboratory capacity for confirmatory testing

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026
Epizootic and human case activity in the Americas
Risk of sylvatic transmission in unvaccinated populations and travelers
Potential for urban outbreak in areas with competent Aedes aegypti vectors
threats.action: Intensify vaccination campaigns in at-risk countries; enhance entomological surveillance; investigate epizootic events in non-human primates as early warning signal

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 documenting elevated case counts
Historically high transmission ongoing across multiple countries
Co-circulation of multiple serotypes increasing severe disease risk
Healthcare system strain reported in multiple jurisdictions
threats.action: Strengthen vector control programs; expand dengue diagnostic capacity; prepare hospitals for surge in severe dengue cases; issue travel advisories

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Dual PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating resurgence
Elevated incidence across multiple countries in the Americas
Vaccine coverage gaps identified as contributing factor
Risk to infants too young to be fully vaccinated
threats.action: Review and strengthen immunization coverage especially in infants and pregnant women; investigate potential waning immunity; enhance laboratory surveillance for vaccine strain divergence

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026
Active transmission reported across the region
Expanding geographic range coinciding with Aedes vector distribution
Co-circulation with dengue complicating clinical diagnosis
threats.action: Strengthen integrated vector management; improve differential diagnostic capacity for arboviral diseases; monitor for potential introduction into new geographic areas

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026
Importation and local transmission risk in populations with coverage gaps
Post-COVID immunization catch-up programs remain incomplete
Risk of re-establishment in previously elimination-certified countries
threats.action: Conduct supplemental immunization activities in low-coverage areas; strengthen surveillance for febrile rash illness; verify immunity status of travelers to affected regions

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025
Seasonal rodent population dynamics increasing human exposure risk
High case fatality rate with no specific antiviral treatment
Potential for person-to-person transmission with Andes virus clade
threats.action: Issue public health advisories on rodent exposure prevention; strengthen reporting and laboratory confirmation capacity; monitor for Andes virus person-to-person transmission clusters

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3/BSL-4 select agents were identified in the surveillance data. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is flagged as Critical given its ongoing zoonotic activity in the Americas across multiple reporting periods (November 2025 and March 2026), its pandemic potential, and high human case fatality rate. Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is flagged as Elevated, with PAHO confirming continued transmission in the Americas as of April 2026, representing a sustained BSL-3 pathogen risk requiring enhanced containment and vaccination response.

diseases: Multiple communicable disease threats (ECDC weekly reports)

amrSignals: No explicit AMR signals detected in available report titles; Bordetella pertussis surveillance should include monitoring for macrolide resistance given resurgence signals; Influenza antiviral resistance surveillance (oseltamivir) warranted given H5N1 activity
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous co-circulation of multiple respiratory pathogens (influenza, RSV) creating compounded healthcare burden in both hemispheres
Resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) suggesting immunization coverage gaps persisting post-COVID pandemic
Sustained multi-year H5N1 activity in the Americas indicating enzootic establishment rather than isolated incursion events
Concurrent arboviral alerts (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) suggesting favorable vector conditions and possible range expansion
Non-infectious public health threats emerging alongside biological threats (methanol poisoning, GLP-1 medication misuse) indicating broader health system surveillance gaps
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset in April 2026 overlapping with Northern Hemisphere late-season activity creating year-round transmission risk
